records.quote:
and there I lay, shaking with terror, and the cold perspiration
pouring out of me
records.paraphrase: The narrator recounts his fear while the lions feed near him.

records.quote:
my experience has been that a round ball from a
smoothbore is quite as effective against a lion as an express bullet.
The lion is soft, and not a difficult animal to finish if you hit him
anywhere in the body.  A buck takes far more killing.
records.paraphrase: The narrator explains his reasoning about firearm ballistics and lion anatomy.

records.quote:
Those people carry the doctrine of the survival of
the fittest to its extreme, you see.
records.paraphrase: The narrator invokes the concept of survival of the fittest to explain the locals' behavior.

records.quote:
the first thing I set to work to do was to try
to make out whereabouts the brutes lay up for the day
records.paraphrase: The narrator describes methodically tracking where the lions rest.

records.quote:
My word!  I did feel queer; I don't think that I ever felt so queer
before.  I dared not move for the life of me
records.paraphrase: The narrator describes his terror and paralysis while the lion sniffs his leg.

criteria.rationale: The only near-scientific references are a passing invocation of 'survival of the fittest' as social commentary and practical remarks about firearm ballistics and lion anatomy. These are decorative or anecdotal, not a material representation of scientific fact, theory, or process driving the story.

Ordinary period firearms (a smoothbore breechloader), matches, and a wagon are contemporary tools of the setting, not speculative or engineered inventions that constitute a novum. A malfunctioning cartridge is mundane hardware, not invention materially affecting a science-fictional problem.
The tale is set in a dated historical past (1869 South Africa) with no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement. An incidental year is not a speculative time setting.
No consequences are developed from an identifiable scientific, technological, or social premise. The 'survival of the fittest' line is a one-off remark, not an extrapolated systematic exploration.

The narrator's tracking of where the lions lay up and his reading of spoor is ordinary hunting fieldcraft, not systematic scientific inference, hypothesis testing, or evidential revision materially advancing knowledge. It is generic investigation.
The story takes place in ordinary terrestrial Africa. There are no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them.

A fever outbreak kills a single kraal's inhabitants, but it is localized background color, not a large-scale disaster that is causally central to the plot. The core narrative is a personal hunting misadventure, not a catastrophe.

candidates.description: The exceptionally large black-maned lion and its family that hunt near Quatermain's wagon and become the object of his revenge hunt.

novelty.rationale: A large lion is an ordinary, if formidable, feature of the empirical African hunting world; it introduces no totalizing or world-altering difference from the authorial norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The animal and the hunt are described in wholly naturalistic, systematic terms (ballistics, lion anatomy, tracking behavior), consistent with a nonsupernatural account.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The lion and the ensuing hunt drive the entire narrated yarn from first encounter to Quatermain's maiming.

estrangement.rationale: The lion evokes terror and awe but remains within the empirical natural order; the estrangement is emotional rather than a novum-driven cognitive dislocation.

candidates.description: The rumored lost white people said to exist in the unexplored African interior, the object of Quatermain's final quest.

novelty.rationale: A hidden lost race could, in the lost-world tradition, constitute a world-altering discovery, but here it is only rumored and never realized in the story; its estranging difference is unconfirmed.

cognitive_validation.rationale: No systematic account of the putative people is developed within the supplied evidence; it remains a frame-story rumor.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The rumored people belong to the framing device only; the substantive narrative is the lion-hunt yarn, which they do not govern.

estrangement.rationale: The lost-race rumor gestures at estrangement but is never enacted or detailed in the narrated events, so it cannot anchor reader-facing contrast here.
